title: PRE-SUASION: An Introduction
coreMove: Shift the planning question from what to ask to what should be made receptive before the ask.
sourcePressure: The introduction establishes pre-suasion as the work done before the request, using the infiltration of persuasion trainings, prepared-ground logic, anchoring examples, and Jim the fire-alarm salesperson with an ethical wrinkle.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Pre-suasion means making a smoother pitch or clever first impression.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a civic-services lead watching residents abandon applications
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the new fee schedule is accepted or treated as another city trick
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead places the rejected form stack beside the revised one before asking staff to notice where people stopped reading
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a counter with two uneven piles of permit forms

exampleSpecs.audience: a bakery owner meeting a hotel buyer before naming the rate
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a high per-pastry price feels premium or inflated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner lets the buyer smell the morning batch beside a sealed grocery pastry before the quote appears
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam lifting from a tray of almond rolls

exampleSpecs.audience: a safety consultant entering a plant where crews distrust outside vendors
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the plant manager grants access before the formal audit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the consultant asks to retrieve a left-behind clipboard, waits for escort approval, then begins only after being walked through the gate like a trusted guest
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard visible through a glass security booth

exampleSpecs.audience: a membership director preparing visitors for a donation ask
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the contribution feels like support for access or a ticket surcharge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director moves the conservation lab photo before the payment screen and watches the same ask land differently
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a faded textile under a magnifying lamp in a framed photo

exampleSpecs.audience: a fitter explaining a premium saddle before stating cost
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the rider hears the price as comfort insurance or upsell
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the fitter has the rider predict pressure points on a sensor map before showing the corrected fit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pressure map glowing red under a rider silhouette

exampleSpecs.audience: a mediator preparing neighbors for a settlement conversation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether both parties enter ready to solve or ready to win
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mediator asks each person to mark one shared cost on a utility bill before the first demand is spoken
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two neighbors seated apart with the same bill copy

skillTargets: identify the before-request condition that changes how the ask is heard
distinguish prepared receptivity from a better pitch
spot the ethical risk in staged trust
choose a truthful anchor before naming a price or request

tryThisNowSpec: Before the next request you plan to make, write the one thing the other person should be noticing first, then choose one honest cue that can make it present before you ask.
